title: Advance Economic Indicators Report (advance goods trade, retail & wholesale inventories, Oct 2026 data) — 8:30 a.m. ET into an NYSE half session
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html re-fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes) and parsed row-by-row across all 179 table rows by this session. The row reads exactly 'Advance Economic Indicators Report (International Trade, Retail, & Wholesale) | November 27, 2026 | 8:30 AM | October 2026', release code A202611270830. Primary-sourced, but filed estimate per the event-research lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep — identical treatment to the sibling advance-economic-indicators-2026-09-30 / -2026-10-28 / -2026-12-28 entries.
notes: DISCOVERED during the thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and it is that ledger's load-bearing find. This calendar already tracked the September, October and December releases of this series and had NO November entry — a hole, not a decision. Why it matters beyond filling the gap: two sibling ledgers (japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-11-27 and this event's own seeding note) described 2026-11-27 as a structurally empty session off which 'no US tape reaction should be read'. Both were written without knowing that Census schedules an 8:30 a.m. ET release into it. BLS is the contrast that sharpens the point: its 2026 schedule (bls.gov/schedule/2026/home.htm, page stamp 'Last Modified Date: February 18, 2026', fetched the same day) runs November 20 -> November 26 (Thanksgiving, no release) -> December 1, with nothing on November 27. So the half session is macro-quiet on the labour side and NOT quiet on the trade/inventories side. Structural context recorded rather than traded: NYSE closes equities at 1:00 p.m. ET that day (1:15 p.m. for eligible NYSE-market options; Cboe's own US-options hours page says 13:00), SIFMA recommends a 2:00 p.m. ET fixed-income close, and the day-after-Thanksgiving session historically runs at a median 0.411x its trailing-20-session volume — so this print lands into roughly half the usual depth with 3.5 hours to price it. Impact is medium, matching its sibling entries; symbols is empty. AMENDED 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research with one fact that changes how the print is READ and nothing about the date: the Atlanta Fed files 2026-11-27 on its GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx `InternalUpdates` sheet — a non-posting date — not `PostedUpdates`, which ends 2026-12-23. So no public GDPNow vintage appears that morning. The ledger's Leg 2 generalises it from the same workbook: across all ten 2026 editions of this series, an AEIR posts only when it is a quarter's FINAL nowcast or shares its morning with a GDP release (02-19, 04-29, 07-28, 09-30, 10-28), and is internal otherwise (05-29, 06-26, 08-27, 11-27, 12-28). That means the sibling advance-economic-indicators-2026-12-28 entry's framing of internal-only status as a late-December property is too narrow — it is this series' ordinary mid-quarter state, and Leg 3 measures those mid-quarter editions as the LARGER movers of the nowcast's net-exports line (median 0.313pp vs 0.140pp for the posted final-nowcast editions, n=93 vintages). The data still lands in the public workbook afterwards (Leg 4); it is the same-day announcement that does not exist.
